title: LOW-AGREEMENT: what predicts the errors the fitted budget is blind to? (zero calls)
question: SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET leaves three wrong calls standing out of fold; the registration read them as LOW agreement. Split the 891 edges at the median agreement and, within the low half, compare wrong-direction against correct edges on every predictor available WITHOUT the key at inference (bootstrap SD, |m|, raw confidence, support, cell tie rate, cell disagreement rate, mean absolute trace-length difference); a predictor works if its CI excludes zero AND it survives a logistic already containing agreement.

outcome_heading: L2829: - **LOW-AGREEMENT (2026-09-14, zero calls): my registered PREMISE was wrong, and correcting it vindicates the ...** (first run; predictor substituted, C-7)
L3099: ## REVIEW of the 2026-09-14/15 session (2026-09-15, zero calls) — three headline conclusions are artefacts

L3215: - **LOW-AGREEMENT, CORRECTED (2026-09-15, zero calls): the registered predictor FAILED and the reported one was the label in disguise. The budget's shape survives on established labels; the top-band drama does not.**

criteria.text: PRIMARY: a predictor works if the wrong-minus-correct difference on LOW-agreement edges has a bootstrap CI excluding zero AND survives a logistic already containing agreement
criteria.value: |length difference| (the REGISTERED predictor) -0.127 [-0.354, +0.088] FAILED; 'length advantage of the ARENA's pick' -0.799 [-0.995, -0.581] is NOT A PREDICTOR (it equals +len_key on right edges and -len_key on wrong ones: its sign IS the label); length advantage of the KEY's pick -0.122 [-0.334, +0.081] null (logistic z -0.7); what survives conditioning on agreement is |mean theta gap| (z -2.9), raw confidence (z -4.8) and marginally the cell tie rate (z +1.8), the first two being what the certificate already thresholds on
criteria.denominator: the low-agreement half of 891 edges: 6 wrong (4 established)

criteria.text: what a two-channel budget would do to the three surviving wrong calls
criteria.value: no second channel is supported (no predictor passed (1)); the premise itself was wrong: the three survivors (0.475, 0.476, 0.605) are ABOVE the 891-edge median agreement 0.441, low only relative to arx/iask at 0.880

criteria.text: the count of wrong edges in the low-agreement half
criteria.value: 6 wrong, 4 established (high half 38, 22); wrong rate by agreement band all(established): 0.00-0.35 5(3) of 328 = 1.5% / 0.9%; 0.35-0.45 1(1) of 129; 0.45-0.55 4(3) of 137; 0.55-0.65 2(1) of 109; 0.65-0.80 12(10) of 120 = 10.0% / 8.3%; 0.80-1.00 20(8) of 68 = 29.4% / 11.8%: on established labels the rate still rises with agreement, so widening with agreement remains the right shape; the '29.4% top band' is 11.8% once the 12 key-indeterminate pairs are removed

roughly 20 wrong edges in the low-agreement half (thin; a null must be reported UNDERPOWERED)

sentence_of_record: LOW-AGREEMENT, CORRECTED (2026-09-15, zero calls): the registered predictor (|trace-length difference|) FAILED (-0.127 [-0.354, +0.088]) and the reported one ('length advantage of the arena's pick') was the label in disguise (+len_key on right edges, -len_key on wrong ones; key-anchored it is -0.122 [-0.334, +0.081], z -0.7); the registered premise was wrong (the three surviving wrong calls sit ABOVE the median agreement); on established labels the wrong rate still rises with agreement (0.9 -> 8.3 -> 11.8%), so the widener's shape stands, but the '29.4% above 0.80' was 8 established of 20. No second channel is supported, on six events: DESCRIPTIVE.

plain_description.what: It looked at the judge's remaining errors that the fitted uncertainty budget misses. Several signals available without the answer key were tested as predictors, including trace-length difference and confidence. No calls were made.
plain_description.why: It looks for a second warning signal for when the arena's call is wrong.
plain_description.information: A working predictor would let the uncertainty margin flag more errors. Result: done, descriptive, after a correction. The registered predictor failed. A reported one turned out to be the outcome in disguise. The premise was also wrong: the errors were not low-agreement ones. No second warning channel is supported; there were only six events. Older p2dca data family: history, not evidence.
